top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks, credited to Katori and Ye, are a mature and experimentally decisive invention: trapping many neutral atoms at the magic wavelength brought accuracy and stability to the 10^-18 level, with demonstrated impact on precision metrology and tests of fundamental physics. The two-laureate allocation and the invention-and-development citation scope are clean, and every member explicitly supports the proposal, so awarding it is clearly preferable to no award.
